mbmm

mbmm implements the Mechanistic Bayes Mixture Model (MBMM) framework described by Do, McCarthy, and Rogers (2026) in Mechanistic Bayes Mixture Models.

MBMM estimates how a covariate changes the probability of a latent biological state expressed through a longitudinal mechanistic trajectory. Examples include productive infection versus non-establishment, or a positive durable antibody gain versus no durable gain.

Rather than reducing a trajectory to a thresholded label, MBMM evaluates each participant against populations of mechanistic trajectories. A covariate-dependent logistic gate supplies the prior state probability, and the trajectory evidence and gate combine into a posterior responsibility. Participants whose trajectories do not settle the state contribute according to that uncertainty instead of being forced into a class.

The package is model-agnostic. Users may supply any positive trajectory function with arguments time and theta, including a custom ODE solved with deSolve. Built-in eclipse-phase viral and prime-boost antibody models are included for the manuscript examples.

The current package provides:

  • censoring-aware participant-by-trajectory likelihoods;
  • integration over latent timing offsets and other nuisance coordinates;
  • entropy-penalised kinetic-population estimation;
  • independent-donor and exact leave-one-out bank construction;
  • Route I state-specific reference banks;
  • Route II restriction to a prespecified parameter-space region;
  • logistic gate fitting, including optional Firth penalisation;
  • likelihood-ratio or penalised-objective statistics with permutation tests;
  • diagnostic plots for banks, responsibilities, and fitted gates; and
  • fully synthetic examples with known truth and executable recovery checks.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("linhdo154/MBMM")

Then load the package:

library(mbmm)

Getting started

The package has four linked vignettes:

  • Should I use MBMM? explains suitable scientific questions, required assumptions, core functions, diagnostics, and reporting conditions.
  • Bring your own ODE reconstructs the built-in models from scratch, shows both familiar parameter boxes and identifiable bank designs, and fits a custom constant-beta HIV model.
  • Route I uses an independent pure reference bank in a productive-infection simulation and checks recovery against known truth.
  • Route II defines a durable-gain state as a prespecified parameter region, uses exact leave-one-out banks, and checks recovery against known truth.

The complete package website is available at:

https://linhdo154.github.io/MBMM/

Minimal workflow 

# Score each participant against each candidate trajectory
LL <- trajectory_loglik(
  obs, candidates, trajectory = my_model, sigma = 0.3
)

# Estimate a kinetic population from an appropriate donor likelihood matrix
bank <- fit_bank(LL_donors, lambda = 1)

# Form the two class likelihoods
l1 <- class_loglik(LL, bank$weights)
l0 <- background_loglik(obs, sigma = 0.3)

# Fit and test the covariate gate
fit <- fit_gate(l1, l0, X)
test <- gate_test(l1, l0, X, B = 999)

The bank used to score a participant must not have been fitted or screened using that participant’s measurements. Use a separate donor sample or exact cross-fitting with bank_loo().

Data and reproduction

No participant-level or packaged SDY2354 dataset is distributed with mbmm. To reproduce the manuscript’s SDY2354 analysis, obtain SDY2354 directly from ImmPort under its user agreement and provide the prepared table to inst/reproduce/sdy2354_table3.R.

simulate_mbmm() supplies a fully synthetic Route I cohort with known latent states.

Citation

To obtain the recommended package citation in R:

citation("mbmm")

The methodological framework is described in:

Do, L., McCarthy, J., and Rogers, B. (2026).
Mechanistic Bayes Mixture Models.
